title: Staged Deployment Guardrails and SLO Matrix for Servable Variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: establish a concrete SLO matrix and staged rollout guardrails for model variant deployments (servable variants) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. This ticket produces the acceptance criteria, automation requirements, and a policy that the rollout service will enforce during canary and progressive ramp phases. Motivation: recent regressions in tail latency and a customer incident during a canary rollout revealed we lack consistent, machine-enforceable gates for latency burn rate and availability. Scope: define per-endpoint and per-tier latency and availability SLOs, error-budget burn-rate thresholds, monitoring signals and alert rules, and the automated actions the rollout service must perform when gates are tripped. Out of scope: kernel-level optimization changes and capacity procurement; those are owned by ENG teams referenced in dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: A published SLO matrix (document + JSON config) that lists p50/p95/p99 latency targets and availability targets for these surface areas: text-generation (short prompt <=128 tokens), text-generation (long prompt >512 tokens), streaming responses, embeddings, and reranking.
Rollout service config schema extended with two new gate types: 'latency-burn-rate' and 'availability-bucket', and an example config for a staged model rollout.

Automation: rollout service triggers automatic rollback or pause when burn-rate > 3 for a 1h window OR availability drops below threshold for 30m; integration tests that simulate gating conditions are added to CI.
Dashboards and SLO alerts: template dashboards created in Console and a runbook that maps alerts to run actions (pause/rollback/notify on-call).
Documentation: PRD + concise playbook published in the internal docs with owner, SLO definitions, and steps for emergency override, and a short FAQ for SEs and customers.
Backward compatibility: existing canary configs continue to work and are migrated to the new schema by the rollout-service team; migration plan approved by ENG owners.
decisions: We will use burn-rate-style gating rather than raw error-budget depletion for automated controls to reduce noisy rollbacks during brief spikes.
Two-tier SLOs: 'Baseline' for PLG/Hosted (lower cost/latency targets), 'Premium' for Dedicated/Enterprise (stricter targets). Each model family will map to a default tier.
Latency windows: p95 is the primary latency SLO for gating; p99 used for observability but not for automatic rollback to avoid extreme sensitivity.
Fallback behavior: when a gate triggers, attempt transparent fallback to a compatible, lower-latency model variant (if available) before full rollback.
tradeoffs: Strict p95 gates reduce customer-facing regressions but increase risk of rollout aborts for low-frequency traffic patterns—mitigated by requiring sustained burn-rate before action.
Using fallback variants may slightly increase cost or reduce output quality; tradeoff documented in playbook and must be accepted by owners per rollout.
Automating rollbacks reduces time-to-remediate but requires very high confidence in our metric signals; we accept a small risk of false-positive rollback and provide fast manual override paths.
notes: 2025-03-12: Ticket created after post-mortem for canary regression incident (link in links).
2025-03-13: PM review with ENG and SRE; ENG requested example configs and integration tests. Added ENG-6123 and ENG-7241 as blockers for rollout-service and metrics infra work.
2025-03-14: Security flagged that automated rollback may interact with audit logging for Private installs; require audit log event on any automatic rollback (added to acceptance criteria).
testing_plan: Unit tests for new rollout-service gate logic.
Integration test harness that replays production-like traffic and injects latency/failure to verify gates pause/rollback behavior.
Chaos test: schedule a job in staging that simulates p95 regression with a sustained period to test burn-rate calculation and automatic rollback path.
Manual validation: SE-run canary with a small number of customer tenants and manual verify of fallback quality before ramping.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dry-run mode (no automated rollback) for 48h with monitoring-only alerts to validate metrics and dashboards.
Stage 1: Canary to 1% traffic with burn-rate gating enabled but configured to 'pause' rather than 'rollback' for first week.
Stage 2: Canary to 10% traffic with automatic rollback enabled and fallback to compatible variant configured.
Stage 3: Progressive ramp to 100% using geometric ramping with checks at 1h and 6h intervals; require green SLOs at each check to continue.
Emergency: immediate global rollback on manual trigger from on-call or product owner if auto actions fail.
monitoring_signals: p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint and model-variant (tags: model.family, region, deployment-mode).
availability (5xx and non-200 business errors) and per-route success-rate.
error-budget burn-rate computed over sliding windows (5m, 1h, 6h) and normalized to traffic volume.
KV-cache hit-ratio and queue-depth as secondary signals for diagnosing latency regressions.
error_budget_policy: Define error budget per tier: Baseline SLO: 99.5% availability monthly (45m/month), Premium SLO: 99.9% (43m/month).
Automated gating thresholds: burn-rate > 3 over 1h => pause deployment; burn-rate > 6 over 1h => rollback and alert.
Grace windows: require sustained violation across two consecutive 15m buckets before triggering pause to avoid reaction to transient spikes.
Quota for manual overrides: product owner may override a single pause per rollout after filling out a short mitigation checklist.
